tasks.task: Establish site, confirm scaffold design, occupancy interface
tasks.scope: Site induction, SWMS review, permit confirmation, scaffold design review with engineer, occupancy restrictions briefing (business hours access), emergency procedures
hazards: Incomplete or incorrect site induction leading to worker misunderstanding of hazards and emergency procedures
SWMS or permit documentation gaps creating uncertainty about scope, authority, or control responsibility
Scaffold design not certified or not matching site conditions, creating structural doubt
tasks.dominant_hazard: Scaffold design certification missing or non-compliant with site loads and geometry
controls: Obtain signed scaffold design certificate from licensed scaffolder confirming design meets site geometry, load requirements, and WHS Reg 2017 Schedule 3 before scaffold erection commences.
Verify scaffold load calculations include anticipated work loads, plant, storage, and occupancy floor loads — check against design stamp and site drawings.
Conduct site induction briefing covering: hazards specific to this project, emergency procedures, occupancy restrictions (business hours access only), evacuation routes, assembly point, first aid.
Review SWMS with all workers on site — confirm understanding of their task steps, hazards, controls, hold points, and stop-work triggers; obtain signed acknowledgment.
Confirm occupancy restrictions in writing with building manager: no work during occupied hours; specify permitted work windows (dates, times); confirm emergency access and evacuation procedures.
Brief all workers on emergency procedures: location of first aid kit and AED, emergency contact numbers, assembly point, evacuation route, rescue procedure if worker injury occurs.
Check that all site permits are signed and held on site: scaffold erection permit (licensed scaffolder signature), working at heights permit, noise management plan (if applicable).
Verify White Card or equivalent induction is current for all workers and held on file before any site work begins.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: licensed scaffolder has signed design certificate and load calculations are certified and approved by project engineer.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker on site until: site induction completed, SWMS reviewed and acknowledged, occupancy restrictions briefing delivered, and all permits are signed and on file.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold design certificate is unsigned, missing, or does not match site conditions or load requirements identified during erection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupancy restrictions are breached (work occurring during occupied hours) or no confirmation exists from building manager of permitted work windows.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker cannot demonstrate understanding of emergency procedures or SWMS controls after induction.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Isolate and barricade occupied floors; establish no-overhead-work protocols
tasks.scope: Confirm ground and first-floor access restrictions during business hours, erect barriers below scaffold, establish two-way radio communication between scaffold and ground, post warning signs at entry points, confirm occupant notification procedure
hazards: Dropped object from scaffold striking occupants on ground or first floor during work hours
Occupants entering barricaded areas and coming into contact with falling debris or hazardous dust
Communication failure between scaffold crew and ground spotter resulting in unsafe movement or dropped loads
Inadequate warning signage or barrier positioning allowing unauthorized access under overhead work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dropped object striking occupant in occupied building
controls: Barricade ground floor and first floor beneath scaffold using solid barriers (plywood sheets or certified drop-protection netting) — minimum 2.4 m height — before any elevated work starts.
Post warning signs at all entry points to barricaded areas stating 'NO ENTRY — Overhead Work in Progress' with pictogram — minimum A3 size — visible from 3 m away.

Establish two-way radio communication between scaffold crew (crew member at platform) and ground spotter — test transmission before each work shift — ground spotter must acknowledge all tool movements.
Confirm occupant notification procedure in writing — building manager to brief all occupants of barricaded floors on entry restrictions and work hours — retain signed acknowledgement on site.
Designate ground spotter during all elevated work — spotter positioned within clear line of sight of scaffold work area — spotter to prohibit entry to barricaded zone and monitor for dropped objects.
Restrict elevated work to nominated hours agreed with building management — no work outside those hours — post hours on signage at entry points.
Remove or secure all loose items from scaffold platform before each work session — tools, adhesive packs, offcuts — store in tool bags or attach with lanyards to prevent drop.
Brief all workers on site before starting elevated work — confirm barricade location, radio procedure, spotter role, and entry restriction — record names and date on site.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start elevated work until: barricades erected to full 2.4 m height below scaffold footprint and building manager has signed occupant notification acknowledgement.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start elevated work until: two-way radio communication tested and ground spotter confirmed in position with clear line of sight to scaffold platform.

🛑 STOP WORK if: two-way radio communication fails or ground spotter loses line of sight — restore communication and spotter positioning before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant enters or attempts to enter barricaded zone — confirm entry restriction and re-brief building manager before restarting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to all four elevations, install edge protection
tasks.scope: Assemble scaffold frame, install guardrails and toe boards to all perimeters, install netting or shroud to contain silica dust, install exclusion barriers below working areas, sign and barricade ground-level access
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker losing balance or footing during scaffold assembly at heights over 4 metres
Scaffold structural failure — incorrect assembly, missing connections, or overloading during erection
Dropped object — tools, fasteners, or materials falling from scaffold to occupied floor or ground level below
Silica dust inhalation — generation during cleaning and preparation work without respiratory protection
Contact with energised electrical services — scaffold positioned near or touching power lines or building electrical installation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold erection over 4 metres
controls: Do not start scaffold erection until licenced scaffolder has reviewed site plan, load path, and ground bearing capacity with PM on point.
Assemble scaffold strictly to approved design and load calculation — do not deviate from connection type, spacing, or ledger fixing.
Install guardrails (min 1.0 m high) and toe boards (min 100 mm) to all perimeters before any worker enters scaffold platform.
Barricade ground level and all below-scaffold areas with rigid barriers and warning tape — prohibit public and building occupants from entry.
Erect silica dust netting or shroud to all four elevations and roof perimeter before any facade work or surface cleaning starts.
Install exclusion barriers (skirting boards or plywood screens) below all working areas to catch silica dust and prevent drift to occupied floors.
Wet-suppress all substrate surfaces before angle grinding or dry cutting — maintain damp state continuously during cleaning and prep work.
Use dust extraction with RPE (organic vapour cartridge respirator for chemical odours; P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) for silica residual dust post-suppression) — SDS on point of use.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: site engineer or licenced scaffolder approves ground bearing, load path, and tie-back fixings on building fabric
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit worker access to completed scaffold until: licenced scaffolder issues white handover certificate and PM countersigns

🛑 STOP WORK if: worker falls, loses footing, or slip hazard (water, debris, mud) appears on platform — investigate and clear before resuming
🛑 STOP WORK if: silica dust suppression system fails, netting is damaged or missing, or dust is observed escaping exclusion zone
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Expose and prepare concrete facade for repair; remove failed render
tasks.scope: Strip existing damaged render coat, expose concrete spalling and cracks, clean substrate with brush and pressure wash (silica dust control in place), identify extent of crack stitching and patching required, allow substrate to dry fully before repair
hazards: Silica dust generation during render removal and substrate cleaning — inhalation exposure without respiratory protection
Sharp edges and spalling concrete causing cut or laceration during render stripping and substrate exposure
Pressure washing creating slip hazard on scaffold platform and ejecting concrete particles or debris
Vibration from pneumatic or power tools causing hand-arm vibration syndrome with prolonged exposure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Respirable silica dust inhalation during render removal and pressure washing
controls: Wet suppression: spray render surface with water mist from ground before starting removal to suppress airborne silica dust.
Use dust extraction on angle grinder fitted with shroud connected to HEPA-filter vacuum during grinding and cutting.
Barricade exclusion zone minimum 2 m below scaffold platform with shade cloth or barrier netting to contain ejected particles.
Prohibit dry render removal or dry substrate brushing — use damp cloth or brush only when dust generation occurs.
Stop angle grinder if water supply or dust extraction fails — do not continue work until both restored.
Pressure wash substrate at low angle (max 60° from surface) to prevent ricochet and ejection onto workers or occupants below.
Isolate pressure wash nozzle from contact with spalling concrete edges — use low-pressure spray setting on fragile areas.
Allow concrete substrate to air-dry minimum 24 hours post pressure wash before repair commencement — log drying completion on site diary.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start render removal until: scaffolder has signed handover certificate, exclusion netting is installed below platform, dust extraction is tested and confirmed working, and water supply is verified at pressure.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply repair coatings or patching compounds until: concrete substrate is confirmed dry (moisture test ≤4% by calcium carbide method or equivalent), substrate is photographed and cracking extent is approved by structural engineer or building consultant.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression system fails or nozzle becomes blocked during render removal — do not resume until system is restored and dust is re-suppressed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA-filter vacuum loses suction or disconnects from angle grinder — do not continue grinding until extraction is restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: pressure washing creates visible slip on scaffold platform — do not resume until surface is dried and slip-resistant matting is installed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Repair concrete spalling and cracks; stitch major cracks
tasks.scope: Perform crack stitching to structural cracks using mortar and mechanical anchors per engineer specification, patch concrete spalling with proprietary concrete repair mortar, level damaged areas with cementitious patching compound, allow repairs to cure per product data sheet
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — loss of balance or footing on scaffold platform during mortar mixing, application, and curing activities
Chemical burn or eye contact from mortar or cementitious repair compounds
Repetitive strain injury to shoulders, arms, and wrists from manual application of crack stitching and patching
Inadequate curing time resulting in structural failure of repairs — premature coating or environmental exposure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during repair work at height over 4 metres
controls: Obtain engineer specification for crack stitching method, anchor depth, spacing, mortar type, and cure conditions before work commences.
Check scaffold tag, handover certificate, and licenced scaffolder sign-off are visible and current before any worker accesses platform.
Check working at heights permit is signed and current for this specific task date and crew.
Obtain and display SDS for all mortar, repair compounds, epoxy resins, and chemical anchors on the work platform before use.
Verify anchor points for fall arrest harness are independently certified and load-tested to 15 kN minimum; record location on task sheet.
Wear full-body harness connected to independent anchor point (not the scaffold) during all work on platform — no exceptions above 2 metres.
Mix mortar in ventilated area away from platform edge; transport in sealed containers; never store mixed mortar on elevated platform overnight.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl per SDS), eye protection, and hi-viz shirt or vest
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack stitching or patching until: engineer specification is received and reviewed by site supervisor, all SDS are on platform, and scaffold handover certificate is signed and current.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow repair area to be trafficked, coated, or exposed to water until: minimum cure time per product data sheet has elapsed and repair surface is checked for full hardness by supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: fall arrest harness anchor point is not visible, not independently certified, or worker is at height without harness connected.
🛑 STOP WORK if: rain, wind, or temperature falls below 5°C during application or initial cure phase.
🛑 STOP WORK if: SDS is not available on platform, chemical contact occurs, or ventilation fails during mortar mixing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Apply anti-carbonation coating system to all elevations
tasks.scope: Apply primer coat to all prepared surfaces, apply two-pack anti-carbonation sealer system per manufacturer specification, maintain curing intervals between coats, allow full cure before top coat application
hazards: Inhalation of primer and sealer fumes — two-pack chemical system generating volatile organic compounds and isocyanate vapour
Skin contact with two-pack epoxy or polyurethane coating causing chemical dermatitis or sensitisation
Slipping on wet or newly coated scaffold platform creating fall hazard
Inadequate ventilation on scaffold platform trapping solvent vapours during application
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of isocyanate vapour and VOC from two-pack anti-carbonation sealer at height
controls: Obtain SDS for primer and two-pack sealer on point of use before application starts.
Verify substrate is clean, dry, and free of dust, oil, and contamination per SDS requirements before coating.
Mix two-pack sealer strictly per manufacturer ratio and pot life; discard unmixed material after stated pot life expires.
Install mechanical ventilation (portable fan or natural cross-ventilation) on scaffold platform to remove vapours; maintain continuous air movement during and 30 minutes after application.
Wear respiratory protection rated for organic vapours and isocyanates (half-mask respirator with combination cartridge per SDS Section 8); verify cartridge is unexpired and correct type.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl per SDS), hi-viz shirt or vest, and trousers to prevent skin contact with uncured coating.
Apply primer coat in even strokes; allow full cure time between primer and sealer as specified on SDS or product literature.
Apply first sealer coat in thin, overlapping passes; maintain wet edge to avoid lap marks; allow minimum cure time per SDS before second coat.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealer coats until: substrate has been inspected clean and dry, SDS cure window conditions are confirmed (temperature, humidity, weather), and ventilation system is running continuously.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply second sealer coat until: first coat has cured to initial set per manufacturer specification and worker has visually confirmed no tacky or wet residue on surface.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation system fails or air movement cannot be maintained on scaffold platform during or within 30 minutes of application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ambient temperature drops below SDS minimum cure temperature or relative humidity exceeds maximum stated limit during application or cure window.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports dizziness, headache, nausea, or respiratory irritation despite ventilation and respiratory protection in use.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Apply textured acrylic render finish coat to all elevations
tasks.scope: Prepare and apply textured acrylic render finish coat to all four elevations, colour match existing facade where required, make sure uniform coverage and texture finish per specification, allow curing and weathering per product data sheet
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of acrylic render application dust and solvent vapours
Slip hazard from wet textured acrylic on scaffold platform during application
Fall from height during large-area coverage work on all four elevations
Colour mismatch or texture inconsistency requiring rework and extended curing period
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during textured finish application work on all elevations at height
controls: Verify scaffold is tagged safe by licenced scaffolder and handover certificate is signed before any worker accesses platform.
Check all anchor points and edge protection are installed and secure before starting application work.
Wear organic vapour respirator (per product SDS Section 8) when applying or spraying textured acrylic render.
Verify weather window before starting: no rain forecast within 24 hours, temperature 10–25°C, relative humidity <85%.
Confirm product SDS and technical data sheet are on site and accessible to all workers.
Apply render in horizontal bands from top to bottom; do not spray or brush downward into face.
Stop work immediately if wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or rain begins; cover wet render and allow 24 hours cure minimum.
Barricade scaffold platform perimeter with fall-arrest netting or 1.2 m high barriers; check before each shift start.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start application until: scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and edge protection inspection is complete.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply render until: weather window is confirmed (no rain forecast within 24 hours, temperature and humidity within product limits), all SDS requirements understood, and colour sample is approved against existing facade.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h, rain begins, or temperature falls below 10°C or exceeds 25°C.
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is damaged, incomplete, or displaced during work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker reports dizziness, breathing difficulty, or vapour odour exceeding SDS limits — evacuate, ventilate, and investigate before restart.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
